terra.problem: The slow-parade joke puts down the elders and relies on an age stereotype.
Joshua 6:15 covers the seventh day, not the claim that they marched once a day for six days. Joshua 6:14–15 supports the full statement.
Joshua predicts what the men of Ai will say; the text does not establish that they are already expecting a repeat or are ready to see one.
The one-cookie joke does not match the action in the passage: expecting a repeat and being drawn away.
The explanation states what Ai thinks as fact, though Joshua is predicting what they will say.
The explanation states what Ai is thinking and says Joshua is fine. The text establishes neither.
It calls the fleeing and pursuit the signal. The passage says the ambush rises as soon as Joshua holds out his battle lance.
The text does not say the smoke is a signal to the men of Ai or that they see it from far away.
The passage says the king of Ai did not know about the ambush, not that everyone in Ai was unaware of it.
The text says the king saw the Israelites and did not know about the ambush; it does not say what he was focused on.
The passage says no man was left who did not pursue Israel. It does not say nobody at all remained to watch the city.
The text says every man went out after Israel, not that everyone went out.
The text says the men of Ai saw smoke; it does not say that this was when they learned the city had been taken.
The text does not identify the smoke as the first sign to the men of Ai that the city had been taken.
“Everyone else in the fight fell” includes the Israelite forces. The passage says the men of Ai were struck down, while their king was taken alive.
